close_reason: cRLSign enforcement already has #[ignore] tests in §4.7.4/§4.7.5 with documented reason. Tracked for future policy layer.
description: PKITS §4.7.4 and §4.7.5 require that an intermediate with KeyUsage cRLSign=false MUST NOT validate. However, the certs in question (keyUsageCriticalcRLSignFalseCACert) DO have keyCertSign set. PKITS is testing a stricter policy than RFC 5280 §6.1 — the RFC only requires keyCertSign for path validation, not cRLSign. The current #[ignore] annotation and its comment ('RFC 5280 §6.1 only requires keyCertSign') are correct. The issue: the test body asserts result.is_err() but provides no comment explaining WHY we deviate from PKITS here. A future maintainer reading this will be confused. The ignore comment is correct, but the test body should document that our implementation is RFC-conforming and that PKITS §4.7.4/4.7.5 test a stricter-than-RFC policy. This is a readability/documentation issue, not a correctness bug.
title: KeyUsage cRLSign-only intermediate accepted (PKITS §4.7.4/§4.7.5)
